newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance firm merger plan to be issued by Thur.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance firm merger plan to be issued by Thur.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Wednesday that new measures will be introduced soon to strengthen the Thai finance sector, which he said has recovered from its recent turmoil.
Rerngchai told reporters that the central bank will announce a clear guideline for encouraging mergers of weak finance companies by Thursday.

"For small firms refusing to go along with the tide, we will impose tougher supervision. They will not be allowed to expand if their operating capital is not big enough. We will groom them the way we groom bonzai. Their size will be checked," he said.
The shaky finance sector has faced poor-quality asset problems linked to over-exposure in Thailand's depressed property sector.
The troubles were compounded by a recent liquidity crunch arising from a central bank policy to keep interbank rates high in order to counter speculative attacks on the baht.
The Bank of Thailand, in a move to bolster the financial sector, in early March ordered commercial banks and finance firms to increase provisions for poor quality assets.
It also ordered 10 finance firms hit by short-term liquidity problems to raise capital.
"After the merger guideline is introduced, we expect to see the finance sector heading in a brighter direction," he said.
Rerngchai said the sector's liquidity problems had eased, reflected in the narrowing of the spread between interbank and inter-finance rates, which were as wide as 20 percent in early March.
"The central bank still provides the sector with liquidity at a normal level...The liquidity is still there but we just make sure that those who need it will have an access to it," he said.
